name: Burundian Renga Renga
description: Renga renga, a spinach stew, is genuinely more assertively flavored than a typical greens stew - real technique cooks the greens in real palm oil with black pepper and dried fish for umami depth, giving it a stronger, more savory character than simpler leafy green sides found elsewhere.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Crustaceans, crayfish, mixed species, farmed, cooked, moist heat
ingredients_full.note: ground, standing in for dried minced fish

steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the palm oil, 3-4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, black pepper, and ground crayfish, being generous with the pepper, and cook 4-5 minutes.
Add the spinach and simmer 10-12 minutes until tender and well combined.

name: Burundian Ubugali
description: Ubugali, a firm maize porridge, is Burundi's most essential staple, eaten with nearly every meal, real technique beating the cornmeal in gradually to build a smooth, dense texture.
steps_detailed: Whisk about a third of the cornmeal with the salt into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Gradually beat in the remaining cornmeal, stirring constantly, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, until very thick and smooth.
steps: Whisk about a third of the cornmeal with the salt into 1.25 cups boiling water.

name: Burundian Uburobe
description: Uburobe (also called ubuswage), cassava flour cooked into a dough and traditionally wrapped in banana leaf, is a genuine Burundian staple, real technique steaming the wrapped dough so the leaf infuses it with real aroma.
steps_detailed: Mix the grated cassava with a little water into a firm dough.
Wrap tightly in foil (standing in for banana leaf) and steam over simmering water 40-45 minutes until firm.
steps: Mix the grated cassava with a little water into a firm dough.
Wrap tightly in foil (standing in for banana leaf) and steam over simmering water 40-45 minutes until firm.

name: Burundian Agatoke
description: Agatoke, plantain cooked with a real medley of vegetables, is a beloved Burundian dish, real versions including eggplant and leeks alongside the more common tomato and onion.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion 3-4 minutes.
Add the plantain, eggplant, and tomatoes with enough water to just cover, and simmer 25-28 minutes until everything is tender.
steps: Cook the onion 3-4 minutes.
Add the plantain, eggplant, and tomatoes with enough water to just cover, and simmer 25-28 minutes until everything is tender.

name: Burundian Ibiharage
description: Ibiharage, fried beans, is a genuine Burundian comfort food, real technique frying the cooked beans in oil with onion and garlic rather than just simmering them plain.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

steps_detailed: Cook the onion and garlic in the oil, 3-4 minutes.
Add the cowpeas and fry, stirring occasionally, 10-12 minutes, until well coated and lightly crisped at the edges.

name: Burundian Isombe
description: Isombe, cassava leaves cooked with real peanuts, is shared with neighboring Rwanda, real cassava leaves aren't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in for a milder approximation.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion and bell pepper 4-5 minutes.
Add the spinach and a splash of water, cover, and simmer 15-18 minutes.
Stir in the peanut butter and simmer 8-10 minutes more until thickened.

name: Burundian Grilled Fish (Mukeke)
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting Burundi's Lake Tanganyika fishing tradition, real mukeke being a fish unique to the lake - tilapia stands in as a widely available substitute.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
steps: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Burundian Sweet Potato
description: Roasted sweet potato is a genuine dry-season staple in Burundi, real technique roasting until the natural sugars caramelize at the edges.
steps_detailed: Toss the sweet potato with the oil.
Roast at 425F (220C) for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized at the edges.
steps: Toss the sweet potato with the oil.
Roast at 425F (220C) for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized at the edges.

name: Burundian Beef Stew
description: A simple beef stew, common Burundian home cooking, real technique browning the beef properly first to build real flavor.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

name: Burundian Banana Juice (Umutobe)
description: Umutobe, ripe banana juice, is central to Burundian hospitality and ceremonies, real versions pressed from real ripe plantain.
steps_detailed: Blend the banana with the milk and honey until completely smooth.
steps: Blend the banana with the milk and honey until completely smooth.

name: Burundian Tomato Onion Sauce
description: A simple tomato-onion sauce base, used across many Burundian stews.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil 4-5 minutes until softened.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 12-15 minutes until thickened.
